subject: Animation
title: Outsourcing: Animation's Hidden Workforce
description: A fast breakdown of Outsourcing: Animation's Hidden Workforce for builders.

hook.text: Most American animated shows are drawn, inked, and colored by artists in South Korea, India, or the Philippines.

buildup.text: American studios design characters and storyboard scenes, then send the actual animation work overseas.

discovery.text: Outsourcing cuts production costs by 50 to 70 percent, making the volume of modern TV animation possible.

twist.text: The artists doing the work are often paid a fraction of what their American counterparts earn for the same skill.

climax.text: Global outsourcing makes animation affordable but raises serious questions about labor fairness and credit.

punchline.text: Cheap animation has a hidden cost: the artists who make it.

quiz.question: What ethical concern does animation outsourcing raise?
options: Outsourced animation is always low quality
Overseas artists doing the same work are paid a fraction of American rates, raising labor fairness questions
Outsourcing leads to more animation jobs in America
